products.pressure_boundary: Money, status, institutional prestige, token holdings, or prior wins cannot silently increase simulated or future allocation priority; every priority rule is declared and appealable.
rights_counterweights: synthetic data and no production secrets
allocation authority, fairness, starvation, preemption, and appeal receipts
independent simulator cross-check and explicit idealization
research-only labelling and no security substitution claim
success_metrics: reproducibility, assumption visibility, fairness, starvation, and denial-of-service resilience
allocation reason, authority, expiry, replay, and appeal coverage
cross-simulator disagreement and recovery visibility
forbidden_metrics: production security or quantum-Internet readiness claims
products.mvp_boundary: Synthetic discrete-event scenarios and allocation-policy receipts in an open simulator; no QKD purchase, closed runtime dependency, quantum link, production traffic, or real priority decision.
products.release_gate: A policy that maximizes throughput while starving low-status or low-budget requests must be visible as a governance failure rather than declared optimal.
